messages:
Sylvia: Quick thread — want to land a lightweight 'edge pact' that defines the minimal runtime capabilities + lifecycle hooks we expect across hosted / dedicated / private deployments. Keep it tiny (<=10 fields) so adapters can implement it without heavy coupling.

Omar: Nice. Can we make it per-tenant opt-in? I was thinking a small manifest: `handshake_version`, `capabilities: []`, and a few policy enums.

Ben: Main tradeoff: smaller spec = easier adapters, but we risk leaking implementation semantics (telemetry, identity). We should include `observability_sink` and `identity_mode` as explicit fields.

Andrew: How do we express eviction/drain differences? Private customers often want immediate eviction for maintenance, hosted prefers graceful drains. We need a clear contract.

Sylvia: Proposal: add `eviction_policy` enum = {"graceful", "force", "delayed"} + optional `grace_period_ms`. Default = graceful with 30s. Adapters that don't support graceful must return a capability flag `supports_graceful=false`.

Omar: Also add `streaming_shape` capability: {"unary", "streaming", "mixed"}. If adapter only supports streaming, control plane can emulate unary but with latency/cost caveat.

Ben: Draft example manifest (very small):
```json
{
  "handshake_version": "1.0",
  "capabilities": ["kv_cache", "streaming", "graceful_eviction"],
  "eviction_policy": "graceful",
  "grace_period_ms": 30000,
  "identity_mode": "passthrough",
  "observability_sink": "prometheus",
  "egress_controlled": false
}
```

DevX Bot: devx-bot: Added a short draft in the docs repo: https://go/repo/edge-pact-draft (internal). Please annotate. :eyes:

Infra Bot: infra-bot: Note — private/on-prem installs will require `egress_controlled=true` in most cases. That toggles validation for outbound network policies.

Andrew: We should version the handshake (`1.0`, `1.1`) and treat capability flags as additive. Backwards compatibility rule: newer runtimes can set unknown capabilities but control plane must ignore unknown bits.

Sylvia: Agree. Also add `escape_hatch` boolean so control plane can request a passthrough for critical ops (e.g., creds rotation). Only allowed when adapters opt-in.

Omar: Telemetry concern: telemetry fields should be explicit and redactable. Add `telemetry_redaction` = {"none","tenant_id","partial"} and `allowed_tags`: [] so private tenants can opt to block tenant tags.

Ben: Runtime-surface requirement: adapters must emit synthetic metrics mapping (e.g., `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `latency_p50`) so Console can normalize cost/latency across heterogeneous runtimes. If adapter cannot, it must advertise `metrics_compat=limited`.

Andrew: How do we test this? We need a tiny test harness that simulates an adapter returning capability manifests and then runs a few common flows: unary call, streaming call, graceful drain, forced eviction.

Sylvia: Plan: I'll write an RFC with: enums + manifest example + JSON schema + test harness plan + compatibility rules. Target: 2 weeks for RFC, then 1 week adapter PRs for runtime teams.

Omar: Sounds good. One nit: add `cache_affinity` field (none|tenant|global) so we can reason about KV cache eviction semantics across hosting modes.

Ben: +1. Also call out security: `identity_mode` values = {"passthrough","mTLS-proxy","controlplane-proxy"} with clear threat model notes.

Sylvia: Great. I'll include all of these. Anyone want to volunteer to review the RFC early? @Omar @Ben @Andrew @DevX Bot

Omar: I'll review.

Ben: I'll take the test harness sketch.

Andrew: I'll write telemetry/metrics normalization notes.

DevX Bot: devx-bot: Reminder set — RFC draft due in 10 days. :calendar:

Sylvia: Thanks all — I'll drop the initial RFC link when ready and ping here. :raised_hands:
